metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened gate.jpeg in GIMP (2850x5070 RGB), navigated Image menus extensively. Setup downloads only gate.jpeg; no PNG exists on the Desktop initially.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use File > Export As in GIMP to export to a different format. Demonstrated menu navigation capability across all Image submenus.
metadata.explanation: The setup provides only gate.jpeg. The agent must use File > Export As (or similar) to produce a PNG file on the Desktop. Evaluator checks if any .png file exists at /home/user/Desktop (looking first for gate.png, then any *.png). Initial state has no PNG on the Desktop, so the check fails without agent action (negative-control resistance). No postconfig is needed since the agent must perform the export themselves.

llm_judge_reasons: The getter correctly checks for a PNG file on the Desktop, which is the direct observable outcome of the task (exporting gate.jpeg as PNG).
Negative-control resistance is satisfied: the setup only places gate.jpeg on the Desktop, so no PNG exists in the initial state and the evaluator will return 0.0 before any agent action.
The primary check targets gate.png (the expected export filename), with a practical fallback to any *.png on the Desktop to handle alternate filenames GIMP might produce.
The metric function correctly maps has_png == expected_exists (True) to 1.0, and any other state to 0.0.
The evaluator logic covers the full task requirement: file format (PNG) and destination (Desktop).
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The fallback glob (ls *.png) would match any PNG placed on the Desktop by means other than exporting gate.jpeg; in a fully controlled environment this is acceptable, but adding a check that the PNG is non-empty or has plausible dimensions would harden it further.
